transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you in today?

I’m here because flying has started to feel a lot scarier than I think it should. Even just thinking about getting on a plane, I picture this turbulence from my honeymoon flight again. I know people fly safely every day, but it’s still really getting to me.

When you think about flying or are on a plane, do you ever feel sudden intense fear or panic that peaks within minutes, like your heart races, you feel short of breath, or think you might lose control?

Yes, it comes on pretty fast. Like if I’m looking at flights for a conference, or even if I hear a plane overhead, my chest tightens right away and I get this rush of panic. I just feel like I need to close the laptop or get away from thinking about it.
Do these panic attacks happen only when you're thinking about or preparing to fly, or have they occurred in other situations as well?

It really seems tied to flying. Like, if I’m looking up flights for a work conference or I hear a plane go over, I can feel my chest tighten right away and I get this rush of panic, like I need to shut the laptop or get away from the thought. I don’t really notice it happening out of nowhere in other situations.
Because of this fear, do you go out of your way to avoid thinking about flying, looking up flights, or even going near airports?

Yes, I do. I’ve been choosing to drive really long distances instead of flying, or I’ll just turn down work trainings if they would require a flight. And if I absolutely have to talk through a trip, I usually need my husband sitting with me, otherwise I feel like I’ll back out.
When you're not actively thinking about flying or planning a trip, do you still find yourself worrying a lot about flying or feeling on edge about the possibility of having to fly in the future?

Yeah, I do sometimes. Even when I’m not planning anything, the idea that I might have to fly later kind of sits in the back of my mind. I know flying is supposed to be safe, but I keep thinking about that bad turbulence on my honeymoon flight, and then just picturing getting on a plane feels way scarier than it should.
How long have you been feeling this way about flying? Has it been at least six months or more that you've experienced this intense fear and avoidance?
Yes, definitely more than six months. It started after that really turbulent flight coming back from my honeymoon, so… about two years and five months ago now.
Have you ever had a panic attack in situations that aren’t related to flying, like being in crowded places, using public transportation, or during stressful moments at work or home?
No, not that I’ve noticed. It really seems tied to flying for me. I don’t usually have that kind of reaction in crowds or at work or anything like that.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious about flying even when you're not actively thinking about it or planning a trip, like it's constantly lingering in the back of your mind?

Yeah, it does kind of linger. I’m here because flying just feels way scarier than it should now. Even if I’m not booking a trip, just the idea of getting on a plane makes me picture that turbulence from my honeymoon flight again, even though I know people fly safely every day.
When you think about flying or the possibility of having to fly in the future, do you feel a constant, nagging anxiety that isn't necessarily panic, but more like ongoing worry or dread?

Yes, it’s more like a dread than full panic most of the time. Just thinking that I might have to fly again makes me picture that really bad turbulence from my honeymoon flight, and then flying feels way scarier than I know it probably should. I know people fly safely every day, but it still gets stuck in my head.
Does this fear of flying cause you a lot of distress in your daily life, even when you’re not actively planning a trip or thinking about flying?

It’s not like I can’t function day to day. I’m still going to work and handling things at home. But it is starting to get in the way. I’ve passed up some trainings and conferences my supervisor thought would be good for me, because they’d involve flying. And personally, I keep putting off a Florence trip I was really excited about. So yeah, it’s distressing, even if it’s not taking over everything.
Do you find yourself avoiding all thoughts, discussions, or reminders of flying, even small ones, because they bring back that fear or make you feel like you might panic?

I don’t avoid every little reminder, but I do avoid the bigger stuff. Like I’ll choose a really long drive instead of flying, or I’ve turned down work trainings if they would mean getting on a plane. And if I absolutely have to talk through a trip, I usually need my husband sitting with me, otherwise I start wanting to back out.
